Bug_Details:
Optional acts as a container object that may or may not contain a non-null value. It is introduced in Java 8 to help avoid NullPointerException . It provides methods to check if a value is present and retrieve the value if it is present.
Optional is used instead of null values to make the code more readable and avoid potential errors.
It is a bad practice to use null with Optional because it is unclear whether a value is present or not, leading to
confusion and potential NullPointerException errors.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the generated code by using Optional.ofNullable(null), which is unnecessary and can lead to confusion since Optional is meant to handle non-null values clearly.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case triggers the bug by calling the showBug method of the OptionalNullBug class, which uses Optional.ofNullable(null). This results in an Optional that contains a null value, which contradicts the best practices of using Optional.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test passed successfully, indicating that the method'showBug' returned 'Default Value' as expected when encountering a null value wrapped in an Optional. This does not confirm that the bug triggered an error; rather, it shows that the code handles the null case gracefully using Optional's orElse method.
